Only this app may change your dictionaries

Other apps on this phone can reach the dictionary server. With this on, they can look words up but cannot change anything — no importing, preparing or removing dictionaries, and no settings. Turn it off if another app should be able to change things too. Takes effect the next time wuDict starts.
These change how the dictionary server itself runs. Leave them alone unless you know what they do. Anything left empty follows the settings file.

Databases become roughly 3× larger — a 100 MB dictionary lands at about 300 MB. Reading gets slightly faster with no decompression step: expect a few percent, not a transformation. Applies to dictionaries prepared from now on. Default: off.

A search that has to open dictionaries which are not prepared yet stops at this much; the rest are reported as not searched rather than opened. Prepared dictionaries are never capped. 0 removes the cap — one search across a large unprepared library has been measured at 6.3 GB, which on a phone means the app is killed.

What stays open between searches: roughly 350 bytes per headword, so 64 MB holds about 180 000 of them. Past the cap the least recently used are closed and reopened on demand. Higher means fewer reopens and more memory the system will judge this app on.
Each one saturates a core and holds a few hundred bytes per headword while it runs. More is faster and hotter; the phone stays comfortable at 1.
Change only if something else on this device already uses 6888. Page preferences such as theme and panel state are saved per address, so a different port starts them fresh. Default: 6888.
